deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page: no formulas, no derivation and no computation. It is a heavily corrected prose draft, marked 'p.12', of the introductory, methodological part of Riemann's posthumous fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres' (edited by J. Henle and published in 1867 in the Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin). The preceding page discusses synthetic versus analytic methods of research. The following page defines 'Klang' (timbre) as the property of sound independent of strength and direction. It describes the tympanic apparatus as transmitting air-pressure changes to the labyrinth fluid in a constant (amplified) ratio. It then represents timbre by the curve of the logarithm of the rate of pressure change.

Content of this page:
(1) Timbre (Klang) also helps us estimate the distance of a sound source, because timbre changes as sound propagates through air. Riemann remarks that the change in timbre during propagation could in principle be determined by calculation from its mechanical causes. This implicitly points to frequency-dependent attenuation in air, but nothing is computed.
(2) He declines to pursue this further. He only asks of the acoustician (reading tentative) that sound propagation, and by extension the ear's apparatus, cause no large distortions ('Entstellungen', reading tentative) of the timbre. The partly illegible clause seems to say the error never exceeds a certain amount.
(3) Second paragraph: the fineness of timbre perception, directly observable for example in perceiving small differences of pronunciation, is great. Yet estimating differences in timbre always remains very subjective. This sentence reappears almost verbatim at the bottom of the next page: 'Ich gebe übrigens zu, daß die ... dieser Feinheit immer sehr subjectiv bleibt'.
(4) Two abandoned sentence starts: 'Wenn die Feinheit der Klangwahrnehmung ...' and 'so ist dagegen die ...'.

The argumentative role of the page is to set up the empirical premise for the next page. Because the ear discriminates timbre very finely, the middle-ear apparatus must nearly preserve the 'Klangcurve'. That means the ratio between simultaneous pressure changes in the air and in the labyrinth fluid must stay nearly constant. Only a slow variation of that ratio would be compatible with experience.

No implicit mathematical steps need to be filled in.
errors: No mathematical steps, so nothing to check for correctness.
Physically, the remark that timbre changes with propagation distance, through frequency-dependent absorption in air, is qualitatively correct. It is not quantified.

results.what: Qualitative remark that the change of timbre during propagation through air is mechanically determined and computable, and that it serves as a cue for judging the distance of a sound source.
results.modern_name: Frequency-dependent atmospheric sound absorption as a distance cue (spectral distance cue in auditory perception)
results.usually_credited_to: Classical acoustics in general (Stokes 1845 and Kirchhoff 1868 for viscous/thermal absorption); auditory distance cues discussed later in psychoacoustics

results.what: Methodological premise: the fine discrimination of timbre (e.g. small differences in pronunciation) implies that the middle-ear apparatus transmits pressure changes nearly undistorted, while admitting that this judgement is subjective.
results.modern_name: Linear, low-distortion transmission requirement for the middle ear (impedance-matching transformer)
results.usually_credited_to: Helmholtz (1868, Mechanik der Gehörknöchelchen); Riemann's posthumous 'Mechanik des Ohres' (1867)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a prose draft of the methodological introduction to Riemann's known, published, posthumous paper 'Mechanik des Ohres'. It contains no mathematics and nothing beyond what that paper already contains.

checkable.asserts: Context from the next page: scaling the pressure-change rate by a constant c (change of loudness) shifts log f only by the constant log c. The shape of the log curve, i.e. the 'Klangcurve', is therefore independent of sound strength (result 0).

transcription_corrections: Line 1: above the struck 'Das/Der' there is probably 'Die Verschiedenheit' rather than 'die Wahrnehmbarkeit'. The sentence reads roughly: '... Klang dient uns aber [zuweilen] ... die Entfernung der Schallquelle zu schätzen'.
'dass er keine große Entfernung[?] ... des Klanges' should more likely read 'dass er keine großen Entstellungen des Klanges ...'. The word is 'Entstellungen' (distortions), which fits the argument.
'abgleichen[?] und glauben[?]' is more plausibly 'obgleich wir glauben'.
'dass seine Ebene[?] einmal größer ist' is more plausibly 'dass sein Irrthum einmal größer ist' (or 'nie mal'), 'als ein gewisser ...'.
'lässt z.B. in der Wahrnehmung geringer Verschiedenheiten der Aussprache genau, und' should read 'ist z.B. in der Wahrnehmung geringer Verschiedenheiten der Aussprache groß, und'.

The interlinear 'immer sehr subjectiv' belongs before 'bleibt': '... die Schätzung der Verschiedenheiten der Klangfarbe [bleibt] immer sehr subjectiv'. This matches the parallel sentence on the next page.
